- (a) Following approval of the application questionnaire made in accordance with this article, and prior to the issuance of any permit granted hereunder, any applicant seeking to solicit within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County, Georgia, for a commercial purpose shall obtain an occupation tax registration and pay an occupation tax registration fee in accordance with Treutlen County’s fee structure or produce a valid occupation tax registration from Treutlen County, Georgia.

- (b) Following approval of the application questionnaire made in accordance with this article and prior to the issuance of any permit granted hereunder, the applicant shall obtain a regulatory registration and pay a regulatory registration fee of fifty ($50.00) dollars.

- (c) Following approval of the application questionnaire made in accordance with this article there shall be no regulatory registration fee charged for any non-

commercial permit issued to any Treutlen County resident or organization, pursuant to this ordinance.

SECTION FOUR: Issuance of Permit

- (a) Upon qualification and payment by the applicant of a non-refundable occupation tax or regulatory registration fee for commercial or non-commercial solicitation or peddling, where applicable, the Treutlen County Sheriff’s office shall photograph the applicant and provide the applicant with a permit bearing the applicant’s photograph, name, and the name of the organization represented, and identifying the applicant as an authorized commercial or non-commercial solicitor or peddler.

- (b) All solicitors and peddlers permitted by Treutlen County, Georgia, shall carry the permit on their person at all times and said license shall be presented for inspection to any appropriate officer or official of Treutlen County, Georgia, upon demand. The permit is valid only for the locations and duration as approved.

SECTION FIVE: Validity and Renewal of permits

Each permit issued under this article shall be valid only for the person or organization indicated thereon, and until the expiration of the current occupation tax certificate of such organization, where the permit issued is for commercial use, or for one (1) year, where the permit issued is for non-commercial use. Such permit may be renewed upon payment of a fee set forth in Section Three of this article as from time to time established by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners and verification by the Treutlen County Sheriff that the organization represented has renewed its occupational tax certificate for the current year.

SECTION SIX: Display of Permit

The Treutlen County Sheriff shall furnish to each permit holder a device suitable for attaching the permit card to the outer clothing of the permit holder. No person shall engage in any of the conduct authorized and regulated under this article without wearing and displaying the permit in a conspicuous manner.

SECTION SEVEN: Disclosure of purpose of call

At each dwelling, whether it be an apartment unit, mobile home park, or detached single family residence, the solicitor shall inform the occupant in unambiguous terms of the purpose of the call and shall not represent that the solicitor or peddler is participating in any contest, game or other competitive endeavor, or that he or she is offering the occupant an opportunity to participate in such contest, game, or endeavor.

SECTION EIGHT: Posted property

No solicitation shall be made at any dwelling or location where a conspicuous “No Soliciting”, “No Peddlers” or other similar sign is displayed at or near the main entrance or driveway to the premises.

SECTION NINE: Limitations of hours and days for solicitations

No form of solicitation shall occur prior to 7:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p-m. on any given day. No form of solicitation shall occur on any Sunday, unless the solicitation is being made for non-commercial purposes.

SECTION TEN: Exemptions

The following persons and activities are specifically exempt from the requirements of this ordinance:

- (a) Persons, businesses, and organizations exempted from local regulation by operation of state or federal law, or by the Constitution of the United States or the State of Georgia.

- (b) Any employee or officer of Treutlen County, Georgia, the State of Georgia or the United States, or any agency or department thereof, when acting in his or her official capacity.

- (c) Any employee or duly authorized agent of any utility company or provider, provided that the employee or agent is entering upon a dwelling or business location within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County, Georgia in order to perform a service or further a business purpose of his or her employer, in direct connection with the utility service being provided.

- (d) Any solicitor whom is specifically invited by the owner or occupant of a dwelling or business location in the unincorporated area of Treutlen County, Georgia.

- (e) Any religious organization, or representatives thereof, whose sole purpose for calling upon any location within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County is to further the specific religious purposes and goals of such organization and is not for the purpose of soliciting donations, gifts, or contributions.

SECTION ELEVEN: Records of Peddlers and Solicitors Stores of Peddlers and Solicitors

The Treutlen County Sheriff shall maintain records of all registrations made and permits issued and shall keep a record of all complaints that may be made for each peddler subject to this ordinance.

SECTION TWELVE: Enforcement

Enforcement of this ordinance shall be vested with the Treutlen County Sheriff, or any duly authorized deputy.

SECTION THIRTEEN: Penalties and Venue
2:
Any person who violates any provision of this ordinance shall be subject to a fine of up to $1,000.00 and/or imprisonment in jail for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days. Any complaint or accusation seeking the enforcement of this ordinance shall be heard in the State Court of Treutlen County, Georgia.

SECTION FOURTEEN: Severability

If any part or portion of this ordinance shall be ruled invalid, unconstitutional, or otherwise unlawful, the remaining body of the ordinance shall remain in full force and effect.

SECTION FIFTEEN: Repealer Clause

This ordinance effectively and immediately replaces and otherwise repeals any Prior conflicting ordinance of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

SECTION SIXTEEN: Effective Date

This ordinance shall become effective upon passage by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners and the publication of the applicable notice of the same in the Soperton News for four (4) weeks.

This Ordinance is hereby adopted, approved, and enacted this 2nd day of April, 2013, at the regularly scheduled meeting of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County, Georgia.

On April 2, 2013 the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners passed a Peddler’s Ordinance, regulating and limiting the solicitation by salesman, vendors, and organizations seeking any form of financial contribution from all locations within the unincorporated areas of Treutlen County, Georgia. The ordinance requires any such solicitor to file an application for a license with the Treutlen County Sheriff, pay an applicable fee, and subject themselves to a criminal background check prior to obtaining a license, in order to make any form of solicitation within the unincorporated areas of Treutlen County. There are certain exceptions to the ordinance and the ordinance provides for penalties and fines for violations of the ordinance. The citizens of Treutlen County are hereby notified that Treutlen County will begin enforcement of the Peddler’s Ordinance following the publication of this notice. Copies of the Peddler’s Ordinance are available at the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners’ office for inspection and review. Please contact your county commissioner or the Board of Commissioners’ office for further information.

Tom Everett

Treutlen County Attorney
